title: The Dog Chasing a Wolf
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Dog was chasing a Wolf, and as he ran he thought what a fine fellow he was, and what strong legs he had, and how quickly they covered the ground. "Now, there's this Wolf," he said to himself, "what a poor creature he is: he's no match for me, and he knows it and so he runs away." But the Wolf looked round just then and said, "Don't you imagine I'm running away from you, my friend: it's your master I'm afraid of."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Dog doing at the start of the passage?
options: Resting beside his master
Chasing a Wolf
Guarding a flock of sheep
Barking at a stranger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dog think about himself as he ran?
options: That he was too slow to catch the Wolf
That he was a fine fellow with strong, quick legs
That he should give up the chase
That his master would be angry with him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dog say to himself about the Wolf?
options: That the Wolf was too dangerous to chase
That the Wolf was a poor creature who was no match for him
That the Wolf was faster than he expected
That the Wolf belonged to a rival pack

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dog believe was the reason the Wolf was running away?
options: The Wolf was heading home for the night
The Wolf knew he was no match for the Dog
The Wolf was chasing something else
The Wolf was leading the Dog into a trap

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Wolf say when he looked round?
options: That he was tired and needed to rest
That it was the Dog's master he feared, not the Dog
That he was actually faster than the Dog
That he would turn and fight the Dog

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "no match for me" mean in "he's no match for me"?
options: Not able to compete successfully against me
Not interested in fighting me
Not aware that I exist
Not able to see me clearly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Wolf's remark undercut the Dog's boastful thoughts?
options: It reveals the Wolf is fleeing out of fear of the master, not out of fear of the Dog's own strength
It proves the Wolf was never actually running away at all
It shows the Wolf plans to attack the Dog's master instead
It confirms the Dog really is faster than the Wolf

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Wolves are always more cunning than dogs give them credit for
One should not credit oneself for an advantage that actually belongs to someone else
Dogs should never chase wolves without their masters present
Strong legs matter more than intelligence in a chase

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what three things did the Dog admire about himself while running?
options: His fine looks, his loud bark, and his loyalty
Being a fine fellow, having strong legs, and covering ground quickly
His sense of smell, his sharp teeth, and his patience
His speed, his cunning, and his master's praise

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom does the Wolf say he is afraid of?
options: Other wolves
The Dog's master
Hunters in the forest
The Dog himself

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Wolf use to address the Dog?
options: "You will regret this, my friend"
"Don't you imagine I'm running away from you, my friend: it's your master I'm afraid of"
"Catch me if you can, my friend"
"I yield to you completely, my friend"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fine fellow" mean in "what a fine fellow he was"?
options: An impressive, admirable creature
A small, weak creature
A clumsy, awkward creature
A cowardly creature

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the Dog wrong about regarding why the Wolf is running?
options: He assumes it is fear of him, when it is really fear of his master
He assumes it is a trick, when the Wolf is genuinely fleeing
He assumes the Wolf is heading toward him, when it is running away
He assumes the Wolf cannot hear him, when it can

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Dog proudly credits himself for scaring off a Wolf, but the Wolf reveals he fears the Dog's master instead
A Dog and a Wolf become friends after a long chase
A Wolf outruns a Dog and escapes into the forest
A Dog's master orders him to stop chasing a Wolf
